title: Ang 1319–1326: Kalyan
tomorrow: 5 a.m., the car's packed, and someone's at the door. who?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 1312: Kanara's ballad, and Namdev's mirror, one face in every heart. The night raga is done. The next one is short, and comes at evening.
screen: `ONE FACE IN EVERY HEART.` → `A SHORT EVENING RAGA.`

segments.voice: The goodbye dinner is in the backyard: Bebe's saag, string lights her dad put up and pretended were nothing, cousins everywhere, old kirtan playing low on a speaker. Harjit has hardly talked all week. When the cousins leave, he sits on the back step next to Simran with two cups of chai and says nothing for a long time. Then: your Bebe sang me one line when I drove my first long route. He hums it, badly. It's from Kalyan.
screen: `STRING LIGHTS AND SAAG.` → `TWO CUPS OF CHAI ON THE STEP.` → `ONE LINE, HUMMED BADLY.`

segments.voice: Kalyan is a short raga in the Granth, an evening raga of peace, and it opens on ang 1319 with Guru Ram Das. In paraphrase, the first line: no one has found the end of you, Lord. We are your children, and you look after us. You are my great father, and my mother. A short raga, and a very big picture: a parent who never runs out. Here's something to tell a friend tonight. In that one line, God is father and mother both, in a single breath. Peace, in Kalyan, isn't a life without goodbyes. It's knowing the care doesn't stop at the end of the driveway. Harjit says that's what Bebe meant, back then. I can't drive behind you all the way to college, he says. But you're not leaving the One who looks after you. Simran had braced all week for a speech. She got one line, and two cups of chai going cold. So what does a tradition give you for a goodbye? Not words that make it painless. A bigger parent, who goes where you go. Bebe comes out with a shawl, wraps it around Simran's shoulders, and says, in Punjabi, take the chilies too.
screen: `KALYAN: A SHORT EVENING RAGA.` · `WE ARE YOUR CHILDREN.` · `FATHER AND MOTHER, IN ONE BREATH.` · `CARE PAST THE END OF THE DRIVEWAY.` · then, large: `PEACE.`

segments.voice: If you have paper, write the name of someone who has looked after you. Under it, write one thing they did that you never thanked them for. Then set the pen down and sit with that name for the rest of the time, letting the breath be slow and warm.
Ang 1319. Where Kalyan begins: Guru Ram Das's short evening raga, with God as father and mother both.
For tonight: peace, a care that doesn't stop at the end of the driveway. Rest well.
